title: Student Performance Dashboard
context: Group project for Database Concepts & Programming
role: Partner B: frontend and cloud setup
summary: A cloud-hosted analytics dashboard exploring what affects 1,000 students' exam scores in math, reading and writing.

cover.alt: Metabase dashboard with bar charts comparing average exam scores by gender, lunch type and test preparation

media.alt: Full Metabase dashboard titled Students Performance on Exams
media.caption: The finished dashboard: 10 visualizations answering 7 questions

overview: For our Database Concepts & Programming class, my partner and I built a cloud-hosted analytics dashboard using a Kaggle dataset of 1,000 students' exam scores. It shows how factors like test preparation, lunch type, parental education and gender relate to scores.
problem: We wanted to understand which factors outside the classroom influence student performance, and what the data says about unequal access to academic resources. That meant putting the data in a secure cloud database and building a visual layer that makes the patterns easy to read.
contributions: Set up a Linux virtual machine on Google Compute Engine from the command line, with a startup script that installed Metabase automatically.
Reserved a static IP address so the dashboard's address never changed, and attached it to the VM.
Wrote a firewall rule that only let our two home networks reach Metabase, instead of opening it to the whole internet.
Connected Metabase to our Cloud SQL MySQL database over an encrypted SSL connection, using a dedicated database account.
Designed 10 visualizations (bar charts, row charts, tables, a donut chart and a summary number) answering 7 research questions.
teamNote: My partner, Anusuya Thapa, built the backend: the Cloud SQL database, schema, views, stored procedures and backups.

highlights.title: What the data showed
items: Students who completed the test preparation course scored higher in all three subjects.
Students on free or reduced lunch (35.5% of the dataset) scored lower on average than students on standard lunch.
Students whose parents held a master's degree scored highest; those whose parents held a high school diploma scored lowest.
Only 19.3% of students (193 of 1,000) scored above 80 in math.
60.4% of students (604 of 1,000) scored higher in reading than in math.

learned: I learned to provision and secure cloud infrastructure from the command line, connect an analytics tool to a managed database, and turn raw data into charts that answer specific questions. I also practiced splitting frontend and backend work cleanly with a partner.

title: Reading Journal
context: Solo project for MAC 220, Android App Development
summary: An Android app for keeping a personal record of every book you finish: the cover, your rating, favorite quote, review and notes.

cover.alt: Reading Journal app showing a list of book cards with covers, authors and ratings

media.alt: Scrolling through the list of saved books
media.caption: Browsing saved books

media.alt: Filling in a new journal entry with a cover, rating and review
media.caption: Adding an entry

media.alt: Opening a book's full journal entry
media.caption: Viewing an entry

media.alt: Confirmation dialog asking whether to delete the journal entry
media.caption: Delete confirmation

overview: Reading Journal is an Android app for keeping a personal record of every book you finish. Each entry holds the cover, title, author, a star rating, a favorite quote, a summary, a review and personal notes.
problem: I combined two of my favorite hobbies, reading and journaling. I already highlight passages and save notes on my Kindle, and journaling helps me sort out my thoughts. I wanted one simple place to remember why I loved a book, or why I didn't.
contributions: Built three screens as fragments (the book list, the add/edit form and the book detail view), with back navigation between them.
Used a ViewModel and LiveData to keep book data separate from the screens, so the list updates itself whenever a book is added, edited or deleted.
Saved entries on the device as JSON in SharedPreferences, so they're still there after the app is closed.
Let users pick a cover image from their phone and rate books in half-star steps.
Required a title before an entry can be saved.

highlights.title: Challenges I solved
items: Keeping cover images: Android can block access to a chosen photo later, so the app asks to keep permission for it, and shows a placeholder if the image still can't load.
Accidental deletes: Edit and Delete sat side by side, so I added a confirmation pop-up before anything is deleted.

learned: I'm proud that I built it around hobbies I love and kept it simple and easy to use. Next, I'd like to add genre categories, sections for book series, and cloud sync so the journal works across devices.

title: ThinkFast
context: Group project for System Analysis & Design
summary: A pop quiz game that makes studying more engaging, with quizzes across science, math, computer science, history, music and general knowledge.
overview: ThinkFast is a web-based pop quiz game designed to make learning more engaging. Users test their knowledge across subjects including science, mathematics, computer science, history, music and general knowledge.
problem: Students and lifelong learners can struggle to stay focused when studying. ThinkFast turns knowledge checks into a game, with feedback on how you did.
contributions: Structured the web pages and app content in HTML.
Worked on styling and layout in CSS to build the interface.
Helped build the feature that lets players revisit questions they answered incorrectly, added after feedback from our stakeholders.
teamNote: I worked with another developer on most of the code.

highlights.title: How we planned it
items: SWOT analysis of the proposed system.
Decision trees and decision tables to model quiz results.
Context-level diagrams of how the system works.
Gantt charts and sprint planning in ProjectLibre.

learned: This project gave me experience collaborating on a web app from planning and design through implementation and deployment, and building a feature in response to stakeholder feedback.
